q: What is the diagnosis? Describe the image.
a:
Osteoporosis

Annotated: Reduced bone density

Increased bone transparency (reduced density), thinned cortex, coarse vertical trabeculae; spine: biconcave/wedge/flat vertebrae, framed ("rim") vertebrae, Schmorl nodules. Loss of mineral with a normal protein matrix.

Annotated: Clear osteolytic lesions

q: What is the diagnosis? Describe the image.
a:
Spondylolisthesis

Forward slip of a vertebral body over the one below (L4/L5, L5/S1) – due to spondylolysis (pars interarticularis defect) or degeneration; graded by Meyerding.

q: What is the diagnosis? Describe the image.
a:
Chondromatosis

Annotated: Loose bodies in synovial

Synovial chondromatosis: multiple calcified loose bodies of similar size within the joint.

q: What is the diagnosis? Describe the image.
a:
Rupture of cruciate ligament

MRI: discontinuous, wavy, oedematous (T2 hyperintense) cruciate ligament – ACL tear (bone bruises, anterior tibial translation).

q: What is the diagnosis? Describe the image.
a:
Achilles tendon rupture

MRI/US: discontinuity of the Achilles tendon with a fluid/haematoma gap (T2 bright) and retracted ends.

MRI: linear high signal reaching the articular surface of the (dark, triangular) meniscus on ≥ 2 slices.
